candidate_relations.reason: Intraosseous calcaneal lipoma is a different calcaneal lesion from a pedunculated osteochondroma.
Osteochondroma matches the reference diagnosis of the pedunculated calcaneal bony protrusion.
Gastrocnemius equinus was a concurrent mechanical finding and prior surgical target, not the osteochondroma.
Calcaneal stress fracture is not supported by MRI lacking marrow edema.
Tarsal coalition is a different hindfoot deformity and is not described.
Overuse injury is a nonspecific alternative, not the bony exostosis.
Haglund deformity is a related posterocalcaneal bony prominence at a different site from the plantar pedunculated lesion.
Insertional Achilles tendinopathy does not explain the plantar pedunculated bony protrusion.
Chondrosarcoma is the malignant cartilage-cap counterpart and is not supported by the small pedunculated imaging lesion.
The truncated label still asserts osteochondroma based on the pedunculated calcaneal MRI lesion, matching the reference.
Calcaneal spur is a related bony prominence with incompatible morphology relative to a pedunculated osteochondroma.
Plantar fasciitis was the long-standing misdiagnosis; MRI showed no fascial thickening.

case_quality_flags: C010 label is truncated/malformed but clearly asserts osteochondroma from the MRI description
